text: As a Full Stack Developer, how would you ensure your API is secure and performant?
referenceAnswer: Security: use HTTPS, validate and sanitise all inputs, implement JWT or session auth, rate limiting, CORS configuration, avoid exposing sensitive fields. Performance: add database indexes, implement caching (Redis), use pagination, compress responses (gzip), use connection pooling, and profile slow endpoints.

text: As a Frontend Developer, how do you ensure your application is accessible to users with disabilities?
referenceAnswer: Follow WCAG guidelines. Use semantic HTML (button, nav, header). Add ARIA labels and roles where needed. Ensure sufficient colour contrast (4.5:1 ratio). Make all interactive elements keyboard-navigable. Add alt text to images. Test with screen readers (NVDA, VoiceOver). Avoid relying solely on colour to convey meaning.

text: As a DevOps Engineer, how would you set up a CI/CD pipeline for a Node.js application?
referenceAnswer: 1. Code pushed to GitHub triggers a GitHub Actions workflow. 2. Pipeline runs: lint → unit tests → build Docker image → push to ECR/Docker Hub. 3. On merge to main: deploy to staging (ECS, Kubernetes) and run integration tests. 4. On approval: deploy to production with a rolling update or blue-green deployment. 5. Set up monitoring (Prometheus + Grafana) and alert on failures.

text: As a Machine Learning Engineer, how do you prevent a model from overfitting?
referenceAnswer: Techniques: 1. Add more training data. 2. Use regularisation (L1/L2). 3. Apply dropout (neural networks). 4. Reduce model complexity. 5. Use cross-validation to detect overfitting early. 6. Apply early stopping based on validation loss. 7. Use data augmentation. 8. Use ensemble methods (bagging) to reduce variance.

rubric.criterion: Mentions getting more data or augmentation

text: As a Backend Developer, explain how you would design a rate limiter for a public API.
referenceAnswer: Common algorithms: Token Bucket (refills tokens over time, allows burst), Sliding Window Counter (tracks requests per rolling window), Fixed Window Counter (simpler but allows edge-case bursts). Implementation: store request counts in Redis with TTL (key = user IP or API key). In Node.js use express-rate-limit with Redis store. Return 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After header when limit exceeded.

rubric.criterion: Mentions keying by IP or API key
